extracted.intended_audience: guideline developers, guideline reviewers, and organizations assessing clinical practice guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Use the AGREE II instrument to assess the methodological quality and reporting of clinical practice guidelines across six domains and 23 specific items, producing item-level ratings and overall assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 1: Scope and Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall aim, specific health questions, and target population of the guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 1–3: reviewers should judge whether the guideline clearly states its objectives, the health question(s) it addresses, and the intended population.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. The overall objective(s) of the guideline is (are) specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall objective(s) of the guideline is (are) specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate the clarity and specificity of the stated objectives; consider whether the purpose of the guideline is explicit and focused. (Items rated 1–7.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. The health question(s) covered by the guideline is (are) specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The health question(s) covered by the guideline is (are) specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the clinical question(s) or issues the guideline addresses are clearly defined (e.g., PICO elements where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. The population (patients, public, etc.) to whom the guideline is meant to apply is specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The population (patients, public, etc.) to whom the guideline is meant to apply is specifically described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the target population(s) are clearly specified (age, condition severity, settings, subgroups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 2: Stakeholder Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the guideline was developed by the appropriate stakeholders and represents the views of its intended users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 4–6: reviewers should evaluate composition of the development group, consideration of target population views, and clarity about intended users.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. The guideline development group includes individuals from all relevant professional groups.
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline development group includes individuals from all relevant professional groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the development panel had appropriate multidisciplinary representation (clinical, methodological, allied health, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. The views and preferences of the target population (patients, public, etc.) have been sought.
rubrics_metrics.description: The views and preferences of the target population (patients, public, etc.) have been sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether patients/public were consulted or their preferences were considered (surveys, focus groups, representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. The target users of the guideline are clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.description: The target users of the guideline are clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the intended end-users (e.g., primary care clinicians, specialists, policymakers) are explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 3: Rigour of Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Process used to gather and synthesize evidence, methods to formulate recommendations, and procedures for updating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 7–14: reviewers should examine search methods, selection criteria, evidence appraisal, link between evidence and recommendations, external review, and update procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7. Systematic methods were used to search for evidence.
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic methods were used to search for evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether literature search methods are described and appropriate (databases, time periods, search strategies).

rubrics_metrics.name: 8. The criteria for selecting the evidence are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for selecting the evidence are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of inclusion/exclusion criteria, study designs considered, and rationale for selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9. The strengths and limitations of the body of evidence are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The strengths and limitations of the body of evidence are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the guideline reports quality, consistency, and applicability of evidence (risk of bias, study limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: 10. The methods for formulating the recommendations are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods for formulating the recommendations are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the process for moving from evidence to recommendations is transparent (consensus method, voting, grading systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: 11. The health benefits, side effects, and risks have been considered in formulating the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.description: The health benefits, side effects, and risks have been considered in formulating the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether benefits and harms were weighed and clearly documented when forming recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12. There is an explicit link between the recommendations and the supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an explicit link between the recommendations and the supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether each recommendation cites the underlying evidence and the strength of that evidence is indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13. The guideline has been externally reviewed by experts prior to its publication.
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline has been externally reviewed by experts prior to its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether independent external review occurred, who reviewed, and how feedback was addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14. A procedure for updating the guideline is provided.
rubrics_metrics.description: A procedure for updating the guideline is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider if the guideline specifies a review/update timeline, triggers for updates, or processes for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 4: Clarity of Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Language, structure, and format of the guideline and ease of identifying key recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 15–17: reviewers should assess specificity, presentation of management options, and identifiability of key recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15. The recommendations are specific and unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations are specific and unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether recommendations are clearly worded, actionable, and unambiguous (who should do what, when, and how).

rubrics_metrics.name: 16. The different options for management of the condition or health issue are clearly presented.
rubrics_metrics.description: The different options for management of the condition or health issue are clearly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether alternative management strategies are described and compared where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17. Key recommendations are easily identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.description: Key recommendations are easily identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether priority or key recommendations are highlighted (boxed, numbered, summarized) for quick reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 5: Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Likely barriers and facilitators to implementation, resource implications, and monitoring criteria for application of the guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 18–21: reviewers should assess practical implementation advice, tools, cost/resource considerations, and audit criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18. The guideline describes facilitators and barriers to its application.
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline describes facilitators and barriers to its application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether potential implementation challenges and enabling factors are identified and discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19. The guideline provides advice and/or tools on how the recommendations can be put into practice.
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline provides advice and/or tools on how the recommendations can be put into practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence of implementation tools (algorithms, checklists, patient materials) and practical guidance for clinicians/systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20. The potential resource implications of applying the recommendations have been considered.
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential resource implications of applying the recommendations have been considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether costs, staffing, equipment, and other resource needs are discussed or estimated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21. The guideline presents monitoring and/or auditing criteria.
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline presents monitoring and/or auditing criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether measurable indicators or audit criteria are offered to evaluate implementation and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain 6: Editorial Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of guideline content from funding sources and management of competing interests among developers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses items 22–23: reviewers should evaluate influence of funders and disclosure/management of conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22. The views of the funding body have not influenced the content of the guideline.
rubrics_metrics.description: The views of the funding body have not influenced the content of the guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the guideline declares funding sources and documents that funders did not influence recommendations or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 23. Competing interests of guideline development group members have been recorded and addressed.
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests of guideline development group members have been recorded and addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether conflicts of interest were declared and managed (recusal, mitigation, transparency statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System and Global Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are rated on a 7-point scale; AGREE II also includes two global rating items (overall assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items use a 7-point scale from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree'. In addition to item-level scores, reviewers complete two global assessments (overall guideline quality and whether the guideline is recommended for use). Reviewers should systematically apply AGREE II across all 23 items when forming overall judgments.
